title: Threat model for the open core socket; governance claims scoped to their mechanisms
goal: docs/threat-model.md states, from the inspected code, what the open core socket protects and against whom: the assets and key files, the trust boundaries (loopback, LAN, internet; same-user processes; operator versus an agent holding the keys), every listening port with what authenticates it (9090-9094 bearer or roster-bound member signature, 9092 cluster-key signed discovery, 9095 cluster-key sealed gossip bound on every interface, 18080-18084 loopback leaf services), what the bus secret and bearer token protect against and what they do not (a same-host, same-user process reads both), what the HMAC audit chain and commit ledger prove and against whom, what the Wasm (wasmi) cell bounds and that the Docker sandbox_exec path has no implementation in core, that the governance vetoes are pattern-based defense in depth against known-dangerous shapes and not a boundary against an adversarial tool, and the recommended operator posture. Every sentence passes tests/core_docs_promise_no_ui_or_plugins.rs. README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md are a sibling claim; their overstated sentences and scoped replacements are reported for a later landing.

criteria: docs/threat-model.md exists and every sentence passes the core docs promise guard
every claim in the document names the mechanism that backs it (file and function) and states the boundary it does not cross
the governance vetoes are described as pattern-based defense in depth, not as a security boundary

settle_queue in src/cli/tasks_cli.rs resolves the release pid and status paths once instead of spawning git rev-parse twice per poll, so a_deferred_release_returns_before_the_worker_finishes no longer sits out seconds of process spawns under gate lane load (the second ship's only failure)
